slides.texte_overlay:
Truths about male friendship
nobody tells you in your 20s
You will lose touch with some friends, and that's normal. People move, marry, change jobs. Keep the ones who still matter and let the rest go with gratitude.
Most friendships survive on one person making the effort. Be that person for the friends you really care about. Someone has to book the table.
Your best friends in your 30s may be people you haven't met yet. A sport, a job, a neighbourhood. It's never too late to build new close friendships.
Real friends tell you uncomfortable truths. The friend who says "I think you're making a mistake" cares about you more than the one who always agrees.
Before: our catch-ups were always the same stories. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and something new to bring every time we meet.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: our catch-ups were always the same stories. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Now I bring something new every time.

slides.texte_overlay: Doing nothing together is underrated. A lazy afternoon, a long drive, watching the game. Quiet time together builds closeness without any effort.
Friendship needs rituals. A monthly dinner, a yearly trip, a weekly game. Rituals keep friends close even when life gets busy. Put the next one in the calendar.
